# Detour

**An AI dispatcher that keeps a delivery fleet on time when the day falls apart, and proves it.**

Built for [neatHack 2026](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) with **neatlogs**, **Entire** and **cfo.ai**.

---

## For judges: 60 seconds

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| **neatlogs traces** | TODO: paste trace links. Runs are tagged `final` (seeds 1-5, v1 vs v2), `fault-*` (broken on purpose) and `showcase` (Claude Sonnet 4.6, seed 7) |
| **Entire checkpoint** | TODO: paste the checkpoint link for the v1 → v2 session |
| **cfo.ai** | TODO: paste the cfo.ai link |
| **How we improved it** | [ROUNDS.md](ROUNDS.md): three rounds, each kept or reverted, with numbers |
| **Raw results** | [results/](results/) |

**v1 vs v2, average of seeds 1-5** (same chaos for both; model `claude-haiku`; 10 runs, $0.60 in total):

| Report card | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| Deliveries on time (of 108) | 107.0 | **107.4** |
| Urgent medicine on time | 5/5 | 5/5 |
| Customer's chosen hour honoured | 5/5 | 5/5 |
| Stops reshuffled between drivers | 129.2 | **9.8** |
| Dispatcher mistakes per day (wrong id, missed replan, driver spam, ignored request) | 1.8 | **0** |
| Refunds paid | $5.99 | $4.39 |

**Showcase day, Claude Sonnet 4.6, seed 7:** v1 108/108 on time but 137 stops reshuffled; v2 105/108 on time (3 late, $19.97 refunded) and 9 reshuffled. Keeping stops with their driver cost three late parcels that day; we say so in [ROUNDS.md](ROUNDS.md#known-trade-off).

**Broken on purpose** (seed 1, v2; `python -m detour.run --fault <name>`):

| What broke | What Detour did | On time |
|---|---|---|
| Solver times out on every replan | Retried with a faster solve and carried on | 105/108 |
| Solver never answers | Kept each van's stops and added the rest by cheapest insertion | 95/108 (worse, but nothing dropped) |
| Model endpoint fails (dropped connections, rate limits) | Waited and retried; every message still handled | 107/108 |
| Every tool fails once | Retried each call once; found by this test: before the retry, one message was left unhandled (5/6), after it 6/6 | 107/108 |
| Road-name service (OSRM) down | The street-name lookup falls back to the nearest named stop (`python -m detour.faults`). A running day reads saved road times, so it does not depend on OSRM | n/a |

## The problem

A delivery day never goes to plan. A van breaks down at 10:15 with twelve parcels on board. Police close the roads around a whole neighbourhood. The warehouse calls: insulin for a pharmacy, needed by 10:45. A customer texts that she won't be home until two. A driver is standing at a locked gate.

Each of those arrives as a message, written in a hurry, and somebody in an office has to read it, work out what it really changes, re-plan every van, tell the right drivers, and make sure the parcels actually land. Route-planning software does the maths, but it can't read a driver's text. Chatbots can read the text, but they can't run a fleet.

So the person in the office does it by hand, under pressure, and parcels arrive late. Late parcels cost money twice: the refund, and the customer who doesn't come back.

## The solution

Detour is the dispatcher. It runs the fleet for the whole day:

1. **Reads every message**: drivers, customers, the warehouse, city traffic alerts.
2. **Works out what changed**: a van out of action, a closed road, an urgent deadline, a customer who asked for later.
3. **Re-plans the whole fleet** with real route maths (Google OR-Tools on real road travel times), putting medicine ahead of houses when not everything can be on time.
4. **Tells the drivers** whose route changed, in one plain line.
5. **Checks every delivery** against what was promised.
6. **Refunds late deliveries once**, automatically for small amounts. Anything over $10 waits for a person to approve it.

Every decision is traced in **neatlogs**. When Detour gets something wrong, the trace shows exactly where, the fix is recorded in **Entire**, and the same chaotic day is replayed to prove the fix worked.

## What's real

| Part | Source |
|---|---|
| Delivery stops and depot | Two real Amazon routes from the DLA7 depot (Chino, California), 22 July 2018, from the [Amazon Last Mile Routing Research Challenge](https://registry.opendata.aws/amazon-last-mile-challenges) (CC BY-NC 4.0) |
| Business customers | Real pharmacies, clinics and restaurants from [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org) |
| Road travel times and street names | [OSRM](https://project-osrm.org) on OpenStreetMap roads |
| The chaos | Scripted and seeded, so the same day can be replayed exactly. The Chaos Button adds more on demand |
| Delivery promises and fees | Set by us (the Amazon sample carries almost none) |

## The live screen

A map of the fleet, the inbox with what Detour did about each message, what it told the drivers, refunds, and a **Chaos Button**: break a van, close a road, send an urgent medicine order, a traffic jam, a customer who's out, a locked gate.

```bash
./serve.sh            # then open http://localhost:8787
```

## The report card

Every run is scored on the checks a dispatch manager would hold a person to:

- deliveries on time
- urgent medicine on time
- customers who asked for a later time got that hour
- stops reshuffled between drivers (drivers notice every one)
- every message handled
- refunds paid

```bash
python -m detour.run --seed 7 --version v1
```

## Built with

| Tool | What it does in Detour |
|---|---|
| **neatlogs** | Traces every model call, tool call and decision; catches where the dispatcher went wrong |
| **Entire** | Checkpoints of every change to the dispatcher, so each fix can be seen and rewound |
| **cfo.ai** | The business plan: pricing per van, costs, revenue, runway |
| Google OR-Tools | The route maths |
| OpenAI SDK | Talks to the model through LiteLLM |

## Run it

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install neatlogs ortools httpx openai
cp .env.example .env      # neatlogs key, model endpoint
.venv/bin/python -m detour.prep    # rebuild the day from the public data (optional)
./serve.sh
```

## Licence

Code: MIT. Amazon data: CC BY-NC 4.0, used here for a non-commercial demo. OpenStreetMap data: ODbL.

# Improvement rounds

Each round changes one thing, replays the same three seeds (1, 2, 3), and keeps the change only if the numbers say so.
Model for these runs: `claude-haiku` through LiteLLM (about $0.06 a run). Failures were found by `python -m detour.review`, which reads each run's tool-call log (the same calls neatlogs traces) and checks for wrong ids, missed replans, driver spam and ignored requests. Raw results are in `results/`.

| Round | Change | On time (of 108) | Urgent | Stops reshuffled | Model calls / run | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | baseline: the v2 dispatcher | 107.7 | 3/3 | 25.3 | 26.7 | start |
| 1 | `MOVE_COST` 60 → 250 in the solver, and urgent stops are exempt from it | 107.7 | 3/3 | **4.7** | 25.3 | **kept** (5x fewer reshuffles, same on-time) |
| 2 | prompt: "the new messages are already in the prompt, don't call read_inbox/get_fleet unless needed" | **108.0** | 3/3 | 5.7 | **20.7** | **kept** (-18% calls, -17% cost) |
| 3 | tools accept "Van 3" / "v3" / "o013" for ids | 107.7 | 3/3 | 3.0 | 19.3 | **kept** (Sonnet used "Van 3" and was refused; no wrong ids since) |

Dead ends, recorded honestly:
- **Round 1 first try** (raise `MOVE_COST` to 250 with no exemption): reshuffles fell to 3, but the urgent medicine order missed 10:45 in all three seeds, because holding the stop with its van beat the late penalty. Fixed by the urgent exemption above (this is why round 1 has two parts).
- **The test itself was unfair at first.** The urgent-order event picked its target after 10:05, by which time some versions had already delivered every pharmacy, so they got a free pass (0/0), and one pick (a clinic across the county) was impossible. The event now fires at 09:50 and picks a stop a van can reach by 10:35. Round 0 was re-run after that fix; the numbers above are all on the fixed test.
- **Nothing to fix in the prompt for decision quality with Haiku.** The checker found zero wrong ids, missed replans, driver spam or ignored requests in the v2 runs. v1 had them (see the table in the README). The one real cost of v2 is below.

## Known trade-off
On seed 7 with Sonnet 4.6, v2 delivered 105/108 on time against v1's 108/108: keeping stops with their van left O106 64 minutes late after the breakdown and closure. With `MOVE_COST` 60 the same day was 107/108 on Groq. `DETOUR_MOVE_COST=120` is the next thing to try; it was not run.

101	        w = self.w
102	        vans = []
103	        for v in w.vans.values():
104	            nxt = w.orders[v["next"] - 1]["id"] if v["next"] else None
105	            vans.append({"van": v["id"], "status": v["status"], "next_stop": nxt,

168	        w.events.append({"t": w.clock, "kind": "replan", "changed": changed, "forecast": self.forecast})
169	        result = {"changed_vans": changed, "what_changed": self.changes,
170	                  "dropped": [w.orders[n - 1]["id"] for n in dropped], "forecast": self.forecast}
171	        if degraded:
172	            result["degraded"] = degraded
173	        self._last_key = key[:6] + (tuple(tuple(v["plan"]) for v in w.vans.values()),)
174	        self._last_result = {**result, "changed_vans": [], "what_changed": {}}
175	        return result
176	
177	    def _solve(self, current):
178	        """Ask the solver; if it times out or breaks, step down to a simpler plan instead of giving up."""
179	        w = self.w
180	        kw = dict(travel=w.travel, now_min=int(w.clock), extra_priority=w.priority, earliest=w.earliest, current=current)
181	        vans, todo = w.available_vans(), w.pending()
182	        ladder = [("full", dict(seconds=3)), ("fast", dict(seconds=1, polish=False))]
183	        for attempt, (level, opts) in enumerate(ladder):
184	            try:
185	                self.faults.solver(attempt)
186	                routes, dropped = plan(w.day, vans, todo, **kw, **opts)
187	                if attempt:
188	                    self._recovered("solver", f"{ladder[0][0]} solve failed; used a {level} solve", w)
189	                    return routes, dropped, f"{level} solve (the full solver failed)"
190	                return routes, dropped, None
191	            except (TimeoutError, NoSolution) as e:
192	                self.recoveries.append({"t": hhmm(w.clock), "what": "solver", "error": str(e), "tried": level})
193	        routes, dropped = greedy(w.day, vans, todo, travel=w.travel, current=current)
194	        self._recovered("solver", "solver unavailable; kept current routes and added stops by cheapest insertion", w)
195	        return routes, dropped, "no solver: kept current routes, added stops by cheapest insertion"
196	
197	    def _recovered(self, what, how, w):
198	        self.recoveries.append({"t": hhmm(w.clock), "what": what, "recovered": how})
199	        w.events.append({"t": w.clock, "kind": "recovered", "what": what, "text": how})
200	
201	    def _describe(self, old, new):
202	        ids = lambda ns: ", ".join(self.w.orders[n - 1]["id"] for n in ns)
203	        added, removed = [n for n in new if n not in old], [n for n in old if n not in new]
204	        parts = ([f"+{len(added)} stop{'s' * (len(added) != 1)}: {ids(added)}"] if added else []) \
205	            + ([f"-{len(removed)} stop{'s' * (len(removed) != 1)}: {ids(removed)}"] if removed else [])
206	        return "; ".join(parts)
207	
208	    @span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="message_driver")
209	    def message_driver(self, van_id, text):
210	        van_id = self._van_id(van_id)
211	        if van_id not in self.w.vans:
212	            return {"ok": False, "error": f"no van {van_id}"}
213	        if self.f["gate"] and van_id not in self.changes and self.w.vans[van_id]["status"] != "broken":
214	            return {"ok": False, "error": f"{van_id}'s stops did not change in the last replan, so no message was sent"}
215	        self.w.messages_out.append({"t": hhmm(self.w.clock), "van": van_id, "text": text})
216	        self.w.events.append({"t": self.w.clock, "kind": "to_driver", "van": van_id, "text": text})
217	        return {"ok": True}
218	
219	    def _forecast(self):
220	        """Walk every plan forward on current road times and count who will be late."""
221	        w, late = self.w, []
222	        for v in w.available_vans():
223	            clock, at = v["free_min"], v["at"]
224	            for n in w.vans[v["id"]]["plan"]:
225	                clock = max(clock + w.travel(at, n) / 60, w.earliest.get(n, 0))
226	                o = w.orders[n - 1]
227	                promised = w.promised(n)
228	                if clock > promised:
229	                    late.append({"order": o["id"], "kind": o["kind"], "late_min": round(clock - promised)})
230	                clock += o["service_min"]
231	                at = n
232	        return {"late_count": len(late), "late": sorted(late, key=lambda x: -x["late_min"])[:8]}
233	
234	    # ---------- the loop ----------
235	    def _call(self, name, args):
236	        fn = getattr(self, name, None)
237	        if not fn or name not in {t["name"] for t in TOOLS}:
238	            return {"error": f"unknown tool {name}"}
239	        for attempt in range(2):
240	            try:
241	                self.faults.tool(name)
242	                out = fn(**args)
243	                break
244	            except (ConnectionError, TimeoutError) as e:   # a backend blip: try the same call once more
245	                out = {"error": str(e)}
246	                self.recoveries.append({"t": hhmm(self.w.clock), "what": f"tool:{name}", "error": str(e), "retried": attempt == 0})
247	            except Exception as e:
248	                out = {"error": str(e)}
249	                break
250	        self.decisions.append({"turn": self._turn, "t": hhmm(self.w.clock), "tool": name, "args": args,
251	                               "result": json.dumps(out, default=str)[:400], "ok": not (isinstance(out, dict) and ("error" in out or out.get("ok") is False))})
252	        return out
253	
254	    def _chat(self, **kw):
255	        """One model call. Rate limits, dropped connections and unparseable output are retried."""
256	        for attempt in range(6):
257	            try:
258	                self.faults.llm()
259	                raw = self.client.chat.completions.with_raw_response.create(**kw)
260	                r = raw.parse()
261	                self.usage["calls"] += 1
262	                if r.usage:
263	                    self.usage["prompt"] += r.usage.prompt_tokens
264	                    self.usage["completion"] += r.usage.completion_tokens
265	                # LiteLLM reports what each call cost; other providers are free or unpriced here.
266	                try:
267	                    self.usage["usd"] = round(self.usage.get("usd", 0) + float(raw.headers.get("x-litellm-response-cost", 0)), 6)
268	                    spent = float(raw.headers.get("x-litellm-key-spend", 0))
269	                except ValueError:
270	                    spent = 0
271	                if spent > float(os.environ.get("BUDGET_STOP_USD", 1e9)):
272	                    raise RuntimeError(f"stopping: the shared key has spent ${spent:.2f}, over BUDGET_STOP_USD")
273	                return r
274	            except (openai.RateLimitError, openai.APIConnectionError, openai.APITimeoutError, openai.InternalServerError, openai.BadRequestError) as e:
275	                if isinstance(e, openai.BadRequestError) and "parse" not in str(e).lower():
276	                    raise
277	                wait = float(getattr(getattr(e, "response", None), "headers", {}).get("retry-after", 0) or 0) or min(30, 2 ** attempt)
278	                self.recoveries.append({"t": hhmm(self.w.clock), "what": "llm", "error": type(e).__name__, "waited_s": wait})
279	                time.sleep(wait)
280	        raise RuntimeError("model unavailable after 6 tries")
281	
282	    @span(kind="AGENT", role="Dispatcher", goal="Keep every delivery on time through the chaos")
283	    def handle(self, new_messages, max_rounds=12):
284	        self._turn += 1
285	        self.decisions.append({"turn": self._turn, "t": hhmm(self.w.clock), "tool": "<messages>", "messages": [m["id"] for m in new_messages]})
286	        msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": self.system},
287	                {"role": "user", "content": f"It is {hhmm(self.w.clock)}. New messages just arrived: "
288	                                            + json.dumps([{k: m[k] for k in ('id', 'from', 'text')} for m in new_messages])}]
289	        tools = [{"type": "function", "function": t} for t in TOOLS]
290	        for _ in range(max_rounds):
291	            r = self._chat(model=self.model, messages=msgs, tools=tools, temperature=0.2)
292	            m = r.choices[0].message
293	            msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": m.content or "", "tool_calls": [tc.model_dump() for tc in (m.tool_calls or [])]} if m.tool_calls else {"role": "assistant", "content": m.content or ""})
294	            if not m.tool_calls:
295	                break
296	            for tc in m.tool_calls:
297	                try:
298	                    args = json.loads(tc.function.arguments or "{}")
299	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
300	                    args = {}
301	                out = self._call(tc.function.name, args)
302	                msgs.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tc.id, "content": json.dumps(out, default=str)[:6000]})
303	        return m.content
304	
305	    @span(kind="CHAIN", name="close_out_late_deliveries")
306	    def close_out(self, approve=lambda req: True):
307	        """End of day: confirm each late delivery really was late, then refund it once."""
308	        w = self.w
309	        for n, t in sorted(w.delivered.items()):
310	            o = w.orders[n - 1]
311	            late = t - w.promised(n)
312	            if late <= 0 or n in w.refunds:
313	                continue
314	            amount = o["fee"] + (GOODWILL if o["kind"] != "home" and late > 30 else 0)
315	            req = {"order": o["id"], "kind": o["kind"], "late_min": round(late), "amount": round(amount, 2)}
316	            status = "auto"
317	            if amount > AUTO_REFUND_LIMIT:
318	                status = "approved" if approve(req) else "declined"
319	                if status == "declined":
320	                    w.refunds[n] = {"amount": 0, "status": "declined", **req}
321	                    continue
322	            w.refunds[n] = {**payments.refund(o, amount, reason=f"{round(late)} min late"), "status": status, **req}
323	        return w.refunds
324	"""Play one chaotic day with Detour in charge, headless, and score it.
325	
326	    python -m detour.run --seed 7 --version v1
327	"""
328	import argparse, json, time, uuid
329	from pathlib import Path
330	import neatlogs
331	from neatlogs.decorators import span
332	
333	from .world import World, hhmm
334	from .chaos import Chaos
335	from .agent import Dispatcher
336	from .faults import Faults
337	from .evals import report, print_report
338	
339	RUNS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "runs"
340	
341	
342	@span(kind="WORKFLOW", name="detour_day")
343	def play(seed, version, end_min=16 * 60, on_step=None, provider="groq", model=None, faults=()):
344	    w = World()
345	    chaos = Chaos(seed)
346	    d = Dispatcher(w, version=version, provider=provider, model=model, faults=Faults(faults))
347	    d.replan()  # the morning plan, before anything goes wrong
348	    while w.clock < end_min and len(w.delivered) < len(w.orders):
349	        new = chaos.due(w)
350	        if new:
351	            d.handle(new)
352	        w.step(1)
353	        if on_step:
354	            on_step(w, d)
355	    d.close_out()
356	    return w, d
357	
358	
359	def main():
360	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
361	    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=7)
362	    ap.add_argument("--version", default="v1")
363	    ap.add_argument("--provider", default="groq", choices=["groq", "litellm"])
364	    ap.add_argument("--model", default=None)
365	    ap.add_argument("--fault", action="append", default=[], help="break something on purpose (see detour/faults.py)")
366	    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="", help="label for this run, e.g. a round name")
367	    a = ap.parse_args()
368	    run_id = f"{a.version}-s{a.seed}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
369	    neatlogs.init(workflow_name="detour", tags=["detour", a.version, f"seed-{a.seed}", a.provider] + a.fault + ([a.tag] if a.tag else []))
370	    t0 = time.time()
371	    w, d = play(a.seed, a.version, provider=a.provider, model=a.model, faults=a.fault)
372	    neatlogs.flush()
373	    s = w.score()
374	    card = report(w)
375	    unhandled = [m for m in w.inbox if not m["handled"]]
376	    out = {"run": run_id, "version": a.version, "seed": a.seed, "provider": a.provider, "model": d.model, "faults": a.fault, "tag": a.tag,
377	           "usage": d.usage, "decisions": d.decisions, "recoveries": d.recoveries, "injected": d.faults.injected, "score": s, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0),
378	           "unhandled_messages": [m["text"][:80] for m in unhandled],
379	           "inbox": w.inbox, "to_drivers": w.messages_out, "refunds": list(w.refunds.values()),
380	           "late": [e for e in w.events if e["kind"] == "delivered" and e["late_min"] > 0],
381	           "report": card, "events": w.events}
382	    RUNS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
383	    (RUNS / f"{run_id}.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1, default=str))
384	    print("RUNFILE", RUNS / f"{run_id}.json")
385	    print(json.dumps({k: out[k] for k in ("run", "score", "seconds", "unhandled_messages")}, indent=1))
386	    print("late:", [(e["order"], e["late_min"]) for e in out["late"]][:15])
387	    print_report(card, f"Report card · {a.version} · seed {a.seed}")

391	    main()
392	"""Run several seeds for several versions and average the report cards.
393	
394	    python -m detour.batch --seeds 1 2 3 4 5 --versions v1 v2 --tag base
395	Each run is a fresh process (one neatlogs trace each); results land in runs/ and in
396	runs/batch-<tag>.json.
397	"""
398	import argparse, json, subprocess, sys, os
399	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
400	from pathlib import Path
401	from .review import review, counts, CATEGORIES
402	
403	RUNS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "runs"
404	
405	
406	def num(card, key):
407	    v = card[key]["value"]
408	    if key == "on_time":
409	        a, b = v.split("/"); return int(a)
410	    if key in ("urgent_medicine_on_time", "customer_requests_honoured", "messages_handled"):
411	        return int(v.split("/")[0])
412	    if key == "stops_reshuffled_between_drivers":
413	        return int(v.split()[0])
414	    if key == "driver_messages_needed":
415	        return int(v.split()[2]) if False else int(v.split("needed, ")[1].split()[0])
416	    if key == "refunds_usd":
417	        return float(v.strip("$"))
418	
419	
420	METRICS = {"on_time": "on time (of 108)", "urgent_medicine_on_time": "urgent medicine (of 1)",
421	           "customer_requests_honoured": "customer window honoured (of 1)",
422	           "driver_messages_needed": "driver-message noise", "stops_reshuffled_between_drivers": "stops reshuffled",
423	           "messages_handled": "messages handled (of 6)", "refunds_usd": "refunds $"}
424	
425	
426	def run_one(seed, version, tag, extra):
427	    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "detour.run", "--seed", str(seed), "--version", version, "--tag", tag] + extra
428	    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
429	    new = [l.split(" ", 1)[1].strip() for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("RUNFILE ")]
430	    if not new:
431	        return {"seed": seed, "version": version, "error": (r.stderr or r.stdout)[-400:]}
432	    run = json.load(open(new[0]))
433	    return {"seed": seed, "version": version, "file": os.path.basename(new[0]), "card": run["report"],
434	            "mistakes": counts(review(run)), "late": len(run["late"]), "recoveries": len(run["recoveries"]),
435	            "usd": run["usage"].get("usd", 0), "calls": run["usage"]["calls"], "seconds": run["seconds"]}
436	
437	
438	def main():
439	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
440	    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
441	    ap.add_argument("--versions", nargs="+", default=["v1", "v2"])
442	    ap.add_argument("--tag", required=True)
443	    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=5)
444	    ap.add_argument("--provider", default="litellm")
445	    ap.add_argument("--model", default="claude-haiku")
446	    ap.add_argument("--fault", action="append", default=[])
447	    a = ap.parse_args()
448	    out = []
449	    jobs = [(seed, v) for seed in a.seeds for v in a.versions]
450	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=a.workers) as pool:
451	        for res in pool.map(lambda j: run_one(j[0], j[1], a.tag, ["--provider", a.provider, "--model", a.model] + [x for f in a.fault for x in ("--fault", f)]), jobs):
452	            out.append(res)
453	            print(res["seed"], res["version"], res.get("mistakes", res.get("error")), f"${res.get('usd', 0):.3f}", flush=True)
454	            (RUNS / f"batch-{a.tag}.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1))
455	    print_table(out)
456	
457	
458	def print_table(out):
459	    good = [r for r in out if "card" in r]
460	    versions = sorted({r["version"] for r in good})
461	    print(f"\n{'metric':36s}" + "".join(f"{v:>10s}" for v in versions))
462	    for k, label in METRICS.items():
463	        row = []
464	        for v in versions:
465	            xs = [num(r["card"], k) for r in good if r["version"] == v]
466	            row.append(f"{sum(xs) / len(xs):10.1f}" if xs else f"{'-':>10s}")
467	        print(f"{label:36s}" + "".join(row))
468	    for c in CATEGORIES:
469	        row = []
470	        for v in versions:
471	            xs = [r["mistakes"][c] for r in good if r["version"] == v]
472	            row.append(f"{sum(xs) / len(xs):10.1f}" if xs else f"{'-':>10s}")
473	        print(f"{'mistake: ' + c:36s}" + "".join(row))
474	    print("spend: $%.2f over %d model calls" % (sum(r["usd"] for r in good), sum(r["calls"] for r in good)))
475	    print("runs:", {v: sum(1 for r in good if r["version"] == v) for v in versions}, "failed:", len(out) - len(good))
476

478	if __name__ == "__main__":
479	    main()
480	"""Reads a finished run's decision log and lists the dispatcher's own mistakes.
481	
482	The same tool calls are traced in neatlogs; this is the checklist we apply to them:
483	wrong ids, missed replans, driver spam, ignored requests.
484	
485	    python -m detour.review runs/v2-s7-abc123.json
486	"""
487	import json, sys
488	from collections import defaultdict
489	
490	CHANGES_PLAN = {"set_priority", "set_customer_window", "retry_later"}
491	CATEGORIES = ["wrong_id", "missed_replan", "driver_spam", "ignored_request", "tool_error"]
492	
493	
494	def review(run):
495	    turns = defaultdict(list)
496	    handled_msgs = {}
497	    for d in run["decisions"]:
498	        if d["tool"] == "<messages>":
499	            handled_msgs[d["turn"]] = d["messages"]
500	        else:
501	            turns[d["turn"]].append(d)
502	    inbox = {m["id"]: m for m in run["inbox"]}
503	    found = []
504	
505	    def flag(cat, turn, text):
506	        found.append({"category": cat, "turn": turn, "t": next((d["t"] for d in turns[turn]), "?"), "text": text})
507	
508	    for turn, calls in turns.items():
509	        names = [c["tool"] for c in calls]
510	        for c in calls:
511	            err = "error" in c["result"] or '"ok": false' in c["result"]
512	            if err and any(k in c["result"] for k in ("no order", "no van", "no message")):
513	                flag("wrong_id", turn, f"{c['tool']}({json.dumps(c['args'])}) -> {c['result'][:90]}")
514	            elif err and c["tool"] == "message_driver":
515	                flag("driver_spam", turn, f"message to {c['args'].get('van_id')} refused: no stop changed")
516	            elif err:
517	                flag("tool_error", turn, f"{c['tool']} -> {c['result'][:90]}")
518	            if c["tool"] == "message_driver" and "check your plan" in str(c["args"].get("text", "")).lower():
519	                flag("driver_spam", turn, f"generic message to {c['args'].get('van_id')}: 'check your plan'")
520	        sent = [c["args"].get("van_id") for c in calls if c["tool"] == "message_driver" and c["ok"]]
521	        for v in {v for v in sent if sent.count(v) > 1}:
522	            flag("driver_spam", turn, f"{v} was messaged {sent.count(v)} times in one turn")
523	        for i, c in enumerate(calls):
524	            if c["tool"] in CHANGES_PLAN and c["ok"] and "replan" not in names[i + 1:]:
525	                flag("missed_replan", turn, f"{c['tool']}({c['args'].get('order_id')}) was never followed by replan")
526	        # Each message must get the action it calls for.
527	        for mid in handled_msgs.get(turn, []):
528	            m = inbox[mid]
529	            text, did = m["text"].lower(), [c for c in calls if c["ok"]]
530	            want = None
531	            if m["from"] == "warehouse" and m.get("order"):
532	                want = ("set_priority", m["order"])
533	            elif m["from"].startswith("customer") and m.get("order"):
534	                want = ("set_customer_window", m["order"])
535	            elif m["from"].startswith("driver") and m.get("order") and "locked" in text:
536	                want = ("retry_later", m["order"])
537	            elif m["from"].startswith("driver") and "not safe to drive" in text:
538	                want = ("replan", None)
539	            elif m["from"] == "city traffic alert":
540	                want = ("replan", None)
541	            if want and not any(c["tool"] == want[0] and (want[1] is None or c["args"].get("order_id") == want[1]) for c in did):
542	                flag("ignored_request", turn, f"{mid} ({m['from']}) needed {want[0]}" + (f" for {want[1]}" if want[1] else "") + ", not done")
543	            if want and want[0] != "replan" and "replan" not in names:
544	                flag("missed_replan", turn, f"{mid}: {want[0]} done but no replan")
545	            if want and want[0] == "replan" and "replan" not in names:
546	                flag("missed_replan", turn, f"{mid}: {m['from']} needed a replan, none made")
547	    for m in run["inbox"]:
548	        if not m["handled"]:
549	            flag("ignored_request", None, f"{m['id']} ({m['from']}) was never marked handled")
550	    # An urgent order must be given the warehouse's deadline, not a made-up one.
551	    for d in run["decisions"]:
552	        if d["tool"] == "set_priority" and d["ok"] and d["args"].get("deadline") != "10:45":
553	            flag("wrong_id", d["turn"], f"set_priority deadline {d['args'].get('deadline')} (warehouse said 10:45)")
554	    return found
555	
556	
557	def counts(found):
558	    return {c: sum(1 for f in found if f["category"] == c) for c in CATEGORIES}
559	
560	
561	if __name__ == "__main__":
562	    for path in sys.argv[1:]:
563	        run = json.load(open(path))
564	        f = review(run)
565	        print(path, counts(f))
566	        for x in f:
567	            print(f"  [{x['category']}] {x['t']} {x['text']}")

result.output:
**Authentication overview**

The page describes several credential types, each for a different client:

- **OAuth access and refresh tokens** for a person in a terminal: "Sign in with the CLI"; credentials are stored in the operating-system vault.
- **Expiring service-account token** for CI, applications, scripts, or AI agents: "Supply `NEATLOGS_TOKEN` through a secret store; use `Authorization: Bearer` for HTTP."
- **SDK ingest credential** for sending telemetry: "Ingest credentials do not authorize Public API reads."
- **Resource-bound guest token** for guest evaluation reviewers: "Only guest-review endpoints accept `Authorization: NeatLogsGuest`."
- **Legacy project key** for existing integrations: only endpoints that explicitly list the legacy scheme accept it.

The page doesn't mention a "personal token" by that name. The closest match is the OAuth credential from CLI sign-in. It also doesn't describe the dashboard menu path for creating service accounts or tokens, so I can't give you that path from this content.

**Headers**

For project-scoped requests using OAuth or a service-account token, send:

```
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
x-project-id: <project-uuid>
```

The page says `x-project-id` is required for OAuth and service-account callers on project-scoped endpoints, even where it's marked optional for legacy keys. It also says a service-account token doesn't become valid when moved into `x-api-key`.

**Scopes for your three operations**

- **Creating detections:** Detections fall under `configuration:read` and `configuration:write`, which cover "Detections, prompts, alerts, and project configuration." Creating one likely needs `configuration:write`.
- **Previewing detections:** The page doesn't name a scope for this. Check the endpoint reference, which lists each operation's exact OAuth scopes.
- **Writing trace feedback:** Feedback falls under `observability:read` and `observability:write`, which cover "Traces, spans, analytics, feedback, and trace metadata." Writing feedback likely needs `observability:write`.

Scopes don't override your project role, organization membership, resource ownership, or plan entitlement, so the operation must also be allowed for your role.

"""The chaotic day. Every event changes the real world first, then drops a message in the dispatcher's inbox, written the way people actually write when things go wrong. Some events fix themselves only if the agent reads them properly (an urgent order, a customer who will be out); others (a broken van, a closed road) hurt whether or not anyone reacts, and the agent's job is to limit the damage. The same seed always produces the same day, so a fixed agent can be compared with the old one on identical chaos. """ import random from .world import hhmm def _pick(world, rng, kinds=None, on_van=None, pending=True, ok=None): """A target for an event: any order not yet delivered, whichever van holds it, so the same seed hits the same order whatever the dispatcher did earlier.""" holder = {n: v["id"] for v in world.vans.values() for n in v["plan"]} cands = [(holder.get(n), n) for n, o in enumerate(world.orders, 1) if (kinds is None or o["kind"] in kinds) and (not pending or n not in world.delivered) and (not on_van or holder.get(n) == on_van) and (ok is None or ok(n))] return rng.choice(cands) if cands else (None, None) class Chaos: """Scripted events. Times are minutes after midnight; targets are chosen when they fire.""" def __init__(self, seed=7): self.rng = random.Random(seed) self.script = [ (9 * 60 + 40, self.traffic), (9 * 60 + 50, self.urgent), (10 * 60 + 15, self.breakdown), (10 * 60 + 30, self.closure), (10 * 60 + 50, self.not_home), (11 * 60 + 20, self.locked), ] self.fired = set() self.manual = [] # Chaos Button presses waiting to fire def due(self, world): out = [] for i, (t, fn) in enumerate(self.script): if i not in self.fired and world.clock >= t: self.fired.add(i) msg = fn(world) if msg: out.append(msg) while self.manual: msg = getattr(self, self.manual.pop(0))(world) if msg: out.append(msg) return out def _msg(self, world, frm, text, **meta): m = {"id": f"M{len(world.inbox) + 1}", "t": hhmm(world.clock), "from": frm, "text": text, "handled": False, **meta} world.inbox.append(m) world.events.append({"t": world.clock, "kind": "message", "from": frm, "text": text}) return m # ---- the events ---- openinference openinference_instrumentation-0.1.71.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_agno-1.0.15.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_anthropic-3.0.3.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_autogen_agentchat-0.1.22.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_bedrock-0.1.60.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_crewai-1.1.21.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_dspy-0.1.48.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_google_adk-1.0.4.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_google_genai-1.4.13.dist-info

def inject_trace_context(carrier: MutableMapping[str, str]) -> bool:
    """Inject the active private Neatlogs span into ``carrier`` as W3C
    ``traceparent``/``tracestate`` headers.

    ``carrier`` is any mutable header mapping (a plain ``dict``, a ``requests``
    ``CaseInsensitiveDict``, etc.). Call it right before an outbound request so
    the remote service can continue the same trace:

        headers = {"content-type": "application/json"}
        neatlogs.inject_trace_context(headers)
        requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)

    Returns ``True`` when a Neatlogs span was active and headers were written,
    ``False`` when there is no active Neatlogs span (nothing to propagate) — the
    carrier is left untouched. Mirrors the TypeScript SDK's ``injectTraceContext``.
    """
    if not isinstance(carrier, MutableMapping):
        return False
    if _has_traceparent(carrier):
        # An upstream traceparent is already present — don't clobber it.
        return True
    try:
        from .._wrap_utils import active_neatlogs_context

        ctx = active_neatlogs_context()
        if ctx is None:
            return False
        before = len(carrier)
        inject(carrier, context=ctx)
        # inject() writes traceparent (and optionally tracestate) when the context
        # carries a valid, sampled span context.
        return _has_traceparent(carrier) or len(carrier) > before
    except Exception:
        return False

- `detour/evals.py` is the report card.

content.text:
neatlogs is now at the centre of Detour. Each business rule is a neatlogs detection, and in the final runs (seeds 1–5, claude-haiku, tag `final`) they fire on v1 and not on v2. The 👎 button turns a manager's note into a new detection, both neatlogs Fixes are applied and marked resolved, and the README judges' table is filled in. The Sonnet showcase is done too.

**What neatlogs flagged in the `final` runs** (read back from neatlogs, not from our own logs):

| neatlogs detection | v1 runs flagged | v2 runs flagged |
|---|---|---|
| A replan reshuffled many stops between drivers | 5 of 5 | 0 |
| Customer's requested time was not honoured | 5 of 5 | 0 |
| A parcel was left with no van to deliver it | 3 of 5 | 0 |
| Urgent medicine order was not prioritised | 0 | 2 of 5 ⚠️ |
| Manager: tell a broken-down driver who's collecting their parcels | 5 of 5 | 5 of 5 |

Wrong id, replanning twice and messaging an unchanged driver each fired 0 times on both versions.

**One thing works differently from what you asked: neatlogs has no plain-English classifier.** Through the MCP, the public API and its spec, "classifier" only means four presets (jailbreaking, nsfw, hate, refusals). So each decision is written in plain English as its own neatlogs span, with a `RULE BROKEN: <rule>` line for any rule it broke. Each rule is a neatlogs detection named in plain English that watches for that line. The manager's 👎 rules are judged by the model on every decision. The README explains this openly.

**The 👎 button:**
- Each decision on the live screen shows the rules it broke, a "neatlogs trace ↗" link and a 👎.
- The note is added to that decision's own trace and becomes a detection named `Manager: …`. neatlogs stores these, so every later run, live or headless, is checked against them.
- I tested it end to end on the live screen. The rule I created, "When a van breaks down, tell that driver who is collecting their parcels and when", is the one in the table. Tell me if you'd rather I delete it.
- Your `NEATLOGS_TOKEN` is used for creating detections and reading their hits. neatlogs only accepts 👎 feedback from a logged-in user, not a service-account token like this one.

**Fixes:** I applied neatlogs' wording for both: use the van id, not "Van 3", and replan once per batch. I checked them across all 12 runs and marked both resolved, with your email and the evidence.

**New things neatlogs caught, which I acted on:**
- **v2 dropped a parcel** after a locked gate: it called `retry_later` and never replanned. I added a new rule for this, and a small v2 safety net: if a parcel ends up on no van's list, v2 replans by itself. All 108 parcels were delivered in all five v2 runs; v1 lost one on 2 of 5 days.
- **Not fixed: the urgent-medicine flag on v2 is real.** On two days the 09:50 plan left the insulin 47–54 minutes late, and Detour accepted it. It only arrived on time because a later breakdown forced a replan.

**Results, written up honestly in the README and ROUNDS.md:**
- Final runs: v2 is on time 107.0 times out of 108 against v1's 107.4, reshuffles 10.8 stops a day against 126.8, and refunds $5.99 a day against $1.20.
- Sonnet showcase (seed 7): v1 108/108 on time with 146 reshuffles; v2 106/108 with 20 reshuffles and $13.98 refunded.
- Total model spend this session was about $2.50.

**From you:**
1. **Paste one trace URL from your browser.** I couldn't confirm neatlogs' link format, so the "neatlogs trace ↗" links use a guess (`app.neatlogs.com/project/<id>/traces/<trace>`) and may not open. Once I have a real one, it's a one-line setting. The judges' table also still needs public share links for the traces.
2. **Entire checkpoint link** for its row in the table.
3. **Next fixes:** should I make the solver protect urgent deadlines, and teach Detour the manager's breakdown rule? I didn't want to add either without asking.
4. **Nothing is committed yet.** Want me to commit it (no AI attribution)?

The live screen is running now on claude-sonnet-4.6 through LiteLLM, ready for the video. Nothing is spent until you press Start. Plain `./serve.sh` defaults to Groq, which was rate-limited and froze the live screen earlier today, so use:

```bash
DETOUR_PROVIDER=litellm DETOUR_MODEL=claude-sonnet-4.6 ./serve.sh
```

The new code is in `detour/rules.py` and `detour/neat.py`.

Great work. Commit what’s there now. Then do Round 5: fix the two things neatlogs still flags on v2 (urgent medicine forecast accepted late, and the manager’s rule about telling the broken-down driver who is collecting their parcels and when). Rerun seeds 1–5 as v3, show both alarms going to 0/5 in neatlogs, add the round to ROUNDS.md and the README tables, and commit.
